title: Composer's Assistant 2 — real inference on real PDMX MIDI (Wave Q — Model Discovery, item 23)
definitionOfDone: real musical input → real model inference → real symbolic output. Four runs, four passes. Not a health check, not a checkpoint download, not an import.

model.revision: v2.1.0 — large unjoined infill model, finetuned_epoch_49_0
model.architecture: T5ForConditionalGeneration, 16+16 layers, d_model 576, d_ff 2304, 12 heads, fp32
model.licenseAudit: docs/evidence/model-composers-assistant-2-audit.json — SHIP_CLEARED on primary sources (code MIT, weights MIT, training data PD/CC0/CC-BY/permitted; Mutopia-dominated). Not lawyer-reviewed.
model.trainingProvenance: disclaimer.txt + acknowledgments.html: Mutopia Project (2,451 links), CocoChorales (synthetic, CC-BY 4.0), Josquin Research Project, named permitted contributors

environment.where: this Windows machine, CPU only — no GPU was used or needed
environment.python: 3.11.9 (venv C:\ca2v; the Modal image pins 3.10 per the release's declared support)
environment.transformers: 4.31.0 (as pinned by the model's own config.json)
environment.runner: the release's own midisong / encoding_functions / unjoined_vocab_tokenizer / preprocessing_functions vendored at the pinned zip; decode reimplemented from rpr_ca_functions without REAPER — the same implementation shipped in services/composers-assistant-worker/ca2_infer.py

task: infill: mask every measure of one track over an 8-measure window; the model receives every other track as context and writes the held-out track. mask_locations = (target track, each measure) — identical to the platform's Tier B arranger task.

runs.input: PDMX Qma11MhFz64u8wRiW1cTZ5VJ4zTQWbYbVHDnMGafAFoaN6.mid — brass ensemble: trumpet(56) 314 notes, trombone(57) 278, tuba(58) 421, horn(60) 313, drums 484; 64 measures
runs.heldOut: tuba (track 2), measures 1–9, 64 human notes on two pitches (E2/B1 = 40/35) in a steady eighth-note pulse following the harmony
runs.reading: Correct role and density (a bass-register pulse, exactly 64 notes) but every note is C#3 (49): above the tuba's register and unmoved by the trumpet/trombone context, which audibly changes chord. A repetition collapse — the case CA2's own nine-retry rising-temperature loop exists for.

runs.input: same file, same tuba task, same window
runs.reading: A moving bass line (E3–B3: 59, 56, 54, 52) mixing quarters and eighths — a real part, sparser than the human's 64 notes and a fifth higher than the human's register. The single-pitch result of run 1 was a sampling event, not a systematic failure.

runs.input: same file; trumpet (track 0, the melodic lead) held out instead, measures 1–9, 48 human notes
runs.reading: Correct trumpet register (E4–D#5) and a real melodic figure — 71/73/68 in sixteenths and eighths — but the same bar is emitted verbatim for every measure (the <extra_id_0> and <extra_id_1> strings are identical). Idiom yes, development no.

runs.input: PDMX QmYR43wBQC3gRc8a5KUjKQMnCYxFLnefChbWdVbaCPHmAE.mid — 9-track baroque ensemble: piano(0) 715 notes, harpsichord(6) 1580, violin(40) ×2, cello(42), string ensemble(48) ×4; 270 measures
runs.reading: Genuine four-voice polyphony — simultaneous 50/69/74/78 on the downbeat, then 61/69/76/81 — across a 38–83 range: a continuo-style keyboard realisation, which is exactly what a harpsichord does in this repertoire. The richest of the four outputs, on the repertoire the model was trained on.

failuresOnTheWay.failure: ModuleNotFoundError: portion — the second real file crashed in preprocessing_functions._equality_measure, which lazily imports the `portion` interval library only when two tracks share an instrument.
failuresOnTheWay.whyItMatters: The first file (five distinct instruments) never reached that code, and a synthetic three-instrument smoke never would either. The Modal image would have built green and failed on real music.
failuresOnTheWay.fix: portion==2.6.2 pinned in the Dockerfile with a build-time version assertion, and recorded in model_manifest.json.

qualityReading.whatIsProven: The pinned weights load, verify, and produce notes from real multitrack MIDI in 6.5–28.7 s on CPU, with register and rhythmic idiom appropriate to the held-out instrument, and real polyphony where the part calls for it.
qualityReading.whatIsNot: Quality. One collapse in four at temperature 1.0; weak-to-moderate harmonic tracking against the context; heavy bar-to-bar repetition. These are single samples read by eye. The judgment belongs to the tournament — N seeds per task, the platform's hard constraints, the music critic and, for the finalists, blind listening.
qualityReading.domainCaveat: Runs 1–2 are brass-ensemble and baroque-ensemble scores — the model's home repertoire. Nothing here says anything about pop, dance or Mizrahi arrangement, which the training corpus does not contain.

benchmarkResult: none yet — the tournament has not been run
nextStep: deploy services/composers-assistant-worker to Modal (pinned image, build-time smoke) and enter it in the per-task tournament against REFERENCE_PART_COMPOSER and CONTEXT_AWARE_ARRANGER on PDMX Tier B tasks.
